@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import typing as t
+
+from .core import augment_usage_errors
+from .core import Command
+from .core import Context
+
+V = t.TypeVar("V")
+
+
+class MissingCallbackLookup(Context):
+    """A :class:`~click.core.Context` whose :meth:`invoke` raises
+    :exc:`LookupError` instead of :exc:`TypeError` when the given
+    :class:`~click.core.Command` has no callback.
+    """
+
+    @t.overload
+    def invoke(
+        self, callback: t.Callable[..., V], /, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any
+    ) -> V: ...
+
+    @t.overload
+    def invoke(self, callback: Command, /, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Any: ...
+
+    def invoke(
+        self, callback: Command | t.Callable[..., V], /, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any
+    ) -> t.Any | V:
+        """Invokes a command callback in exactly the way it expects.  There
+        are two ways to invoke this method:
+
+        1.  the first argument can be a callback and all other arguments and
+            keyword arguments are forwarded directly to the function.
+        2.  the first argument is a click command object.  In that case all
+            arguments are forwarded as well but proper click parameters
+            (options and click arguments) must be keyword arguments and Click
+            will fill in defaults.
+
+        Raises :exc:`LookupError` if the given command has no callback.
+        """
+        if isinstance(callback, Command):
+            other_cmd = callback
+
+            if other_cmd.callback is None:
+                raise LookupError(
+                    "The given command does not have a callback that can be invoked."
+                )
+            else:
+                callback = t.cast("t.Callable[..., V]", other_cmd.callback)
+
+            ctx = self._make_sub_context(other_cmd)
+
+            for param in other_cmd.params:
+                if param.name not in kwargs and param.expose_value:
+                    kwargs[param.name] = param.type_cast_value(  # type: ignore
+                        ctx, param.get_default(ctx)
+                    )
+
+            # Track all kwargs as params, so that forward() will pass
+            # them on in subsequent calls.
+            ctx.params.update(kwargs)
+        else:
+            ctx = self
+
+        with augment_usage_errors(self):
+            with ctx:
+                return callback(*args, **kwargs)
diff --git a/tests/test_missing_callback_lookup.py b/tests/test_missing_callback_lookup.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1861a39
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_missing_callback_lookup.py
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+import pytest
+
+import click
+from click.missing_callback_lookup import MissingCallbackLookup
+
+
+def test_invoke_command_without_callback_raises_lookup_error():
+    ctx = MissingCallbackLookup(click.Command("root"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(LookupError, match="does not have a callback"):
+        ctx.invoke(click.Command("other"))
+
+
+def test_invoke_command_fills_defaults():
+    @click.command()
+    @click.option("--count", default=2, type=int)
+    def other(count):
+        return count
+
+    ctx = MissingCallbackLookup(click.Command("root"))
+    assert ctx.invoke(other) == 2
+    assert ctx.invoke(other, count=5) == 5
+
+
+def test_invoke_plain_callback():
+    ctx = MissingCallbackLookup(click.Command("root"))
+    assert ctx.invoke(lambda a, b=1: a + b, 1, b=2) == 3
+
+
+def test_forward_uses_lookup_error():
+    ctx = MissingCallbackLookup(click.Command("root"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(LookupError):
+        ctx.forward(click.Command("other"))
